references.text: Joseph explains that although his brothers intended evil against him, God meant it for good—to preserve many people alive. This confirms God's providence in using Joseph's suffering for the salvation of His people.
The psalm describes how God sent Joseph ahead to Egypt—sold as a slave—as part of God's plan to preserve His people during the famine.

Stephen's speech mentions how the patriarchs sold Joseph into Egypt out of jealousy, but God was with him and rescued him, illustrating God's providence in sending Joseph ahead to preserve the people.
Isaiah prophesies about a remnant (שְׁאֵרִית) of Israel that will turn back. The term 'remnant' is the same one Joseph uses when he explains God's purpose in sending him to Egypt.
The prophecy that a remnant (שְׁאֵרִית) and an escaped flock (פְּלֵיטָה) will go out from Jerusalem uses both key terms from Joseph's statement about God's preserving providence.
